units: <cite ref="Mishnah Peah 4:3">Peah IV, 3</cite> <he>ע׳ השכחה</he> the forgotten sheaf (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 24:19">Deut. XXIV, 19</cite>); a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="P00280"><he>עוֹמְרִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="P00280"><he>עוֹמְרִין</he></cite>, <he>עֳמָרִ׳</he>. Ib. VI, 5 <he>שני ע׳ שכחה</he> two sheaves left in the field are considered as forgotten (belong to the poor). Ib. 6 <he>שני ע׳ ובהם סאתים</he> two sheaves containing two S’ah between them (the ordinary size of a sheaf being one S’ah). Ib. <he>וכי מרוב הע׳ וכ׳</he> is the privilege of the owner strengthened or infringed by the quantity of the sheaves (irrespective of their sizes)? Ib. V, 1; a. fr. [<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 15">Lev. R. s. 15</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 551">Yalk. ib. 551</cite>, v. <cite ref="P00280"><he>עוֹמְדִים</he></cite>.]

senses.gloss: [the quantity of grain in a sheaf,] Omer, a dry measure, esp. the Omer of barley offered on the sixteenth day of Nisan (Lev. XXIII, 10—14).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 10:1">Men. X, 1</cite> <he>הע׳ היה בא בשבת וכ׳</he> the Omer, when offered on the Sabbath, was prepared by cutting three S’ah-fuls of barley (sifted down to one Omer).
<cite ref="Tosefta Demai 1:28">Tosef. Dem. I, 28</cite> <he>מותר ע׳</he> that which is left over when preparing the Omer.
<cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 10:6">Men. X, 6</cite> <he>הע׳ היה מתיר וכ׳</he> the offering of the Omer had the effect of allowing the use of the new crop in the country.
<cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 10:7">Ib. 7</cite> <he>קידם לע׳</he> before the Omer was to be offered (before the sixteenth of Nisan); a. fr.
